authoredNote: Names and lines transcribed from a measured run and checked against the fixture source. The identity contract is the whole subject of this fixture. The two `lifecycle` blocks are INDENTED, so their startColumn is 3, not 1 — transcribed wrong on the first pass and corrected against the source.
rationale: H3, H4 and H11 (reviews/hcl/master-review.md), three distinct defects with one root. (a) Terraform and the HashiCorp DSLs REPEAT blocks by design — `locals` may appear many times per file, `moved`/`removed`/`import` are one-per-move, nested `lifecycle` repeats — and the leaf name was derived from block type + labels with no sibling disambiguation, so identity collided: 6,897 duplicate pairs over 1,323 distinct keys across 9,079 files, worst `parameter` at 420 (waypoint's label-less repeats). Because `contains` edges dedupe on source|type|target, two sibling blocks produced ONE edge for TWO symbols. (b) A label-less `data {}` produced an EMPTY name, `labels.join(".")` over zero labels being `""`, which also left its child attribute ownerless. (c) Introducing the document root created a further collision the other way: `moved.tf` holding `moved {}` gave the file and the block one identity, at 308 corpus sites. The unsuffixed Terraform address is preserved in `hclAddress`, so nothing about the address is lost.
